claim: The vendored canonical oracle is only usable if checkout is byte-exact; CI on windows-latest proved that by FAILING, and the pin is what caught it.

event.harness_treatment_of_exit_4: hard FAIL, never a skip (tests/run_all.py) — the run went red instead of reporting a parity PASS it had not earned
event.previous_run_for_reference: 39078519776 (commit fed7180, before the oracle was vendored) was success on BOTH runners because F4c exited 3 and the harness printed SKIP

root_cause: GitHub windows-latest images set core.autocrlf=true, so actions/checkout rewrites LF to CRLF for paths git classifies as text. vendor/canonical_malbolge_py/malbolge.py was such a path, so the runner was not running the interpreter whose SHA-256 is pinned; `file` reports 'with CRLF line terminators' for the converted copy.

reproduced_locally.method: clone --no-checkout of this repository, git config core.autocrlf true, git checkout 7e6eb5d
reproduced_locally.without_attributes: vendor/canonical_malbolge_py/malbolge.py sha256 = 4a2a666f7a28562eeded5e462fb2bc05412619341579c258c7417f28b325214e (identical to the hash CI found, so the CI failure is explained, not guessed)
reproduced_locally.with_attribute_star_text: same clone with '* -text' supplied to git before checkout: sha256 = e64af4f0d51712e99fdf205e1a102587e4e52c863302384b5d2599f6edf3222b, `file` reports plain 'ASCII text executable' — the pin matches
reproduced_locally.fix_committed_as: .gitattributes containing '* -text' (every path, not just the oracle: the sealed corpus, fixtures and evidence artifacts are hash-referenced too)

fresh_clone_measured.statement: the vendored oracle makes canonical parity measurable from a clone that has NO sibling checkout at all — this is the CI situation, now verified without waiting for CI
fresh_clone_measured.gate_verdict_line: => PASS (10 cases x 2 cores x 1 oracle(s) = 20 stdout-hash comparisons)
fresh_clone_measured.why_10_not_11: the 11th case needs external_hello_world.malbolge, which lives outside this repository; the gate drops it instead of substituting anything

not_rewritten: evidence/F4C_VENDORED_ORACLE_20261017.hashes.json and evidence/f4c_canonical_parity_vendored_20261017.json are left exactly as published in 7e6eb5d, including that hashes doc's 'ci_effect' paragraph, which described the intent ('both runners MEASURE canonical parity') before the EOL defect was measured. This file is the appended correction of that outcome.
scope: end-of-line handling of checked-out bytes, and the resulting F4c verdict on the two CI runners. Nothing about the cores changed: src/malbolge_free.zig and src/malbolge_core.py are byte-identical to the hashes sealed for entry 24.
not_claimed: no claim that Windows CI is green at the time of writing — this file records the failure and the fix; the green run, if it happens, is verified separately with gh run watch and reported in the ledger.
why_it_matters: independence of an oracle is a property of its bytes. A runner that silently rewrites those bytes has a different interpreter than the one pinned, and parity measured against it would be a verdict about a program nobody reviewed.
